externalReview: Verified the exact 2026–2027 joint Clinical Technology bachelor. The adopted OER Article 7 states 180 EC; Appendix 3 lists KT2755 as 4.5 EC, while current bachelor-linked API item 32312 states 3.5 EC. All other named component weights agree. The new canonical stores the 176.5 EC with undisputed weights and excludes KT2755, preserving both conflicting values and original 181-EC diagnostic evidence internally. The genuine 30-EC minor and 15-EC clinical-technology research component remain distinct. No 1-EC offset, adopted correction or clinical permission is assumed.
academicJudgment: Qualified academic comparison approved in substance for biomedical science with mathematical/computational methods, subject to final publication checks. The nine biomedical foundations/laboratory/regulation/disease courses provide taught medical-science substance. Calculus, linear algebra, signal systems, numerical methods, probability, programming and data/image methods provide a substantial quantitative technical strand. Consumer product design and robotics are specific complements rather than clinical devices or surgery. The absence of integrated medical-engineering, medical physics, patient-care and placement training is a central limitation. This is a meaningful alternative inquiry, not equivalent clinical preparation. Both credible placement weights preserve that limited judgment.

candidateReview: Retained and reconsidered all target-linked interests from the completed source review. The closest response owns the biomedical, quantitative, imaging and treatment-mechanism inquiries to the supported extent. Clinical-device/biomechanical design and patient practice/safety remain separately assessed candidates; neither can form a sufficiently taught 24-course response with the current UCR offering. Consumer design and robot motion do not establish medical-engineering depth, and general methods cannot replace patient-care/safety practice. Alternative 2 fails substantive feasibility; stop at one.
alignmentReview: Each stored external component and each scheduled UCR course has one row. The eleven positive relationships specify the addressed part and excluded clinical/integrated scope. Later repeated clinical-system units, skills/safety, device design, placement and research are not forced into general-method matches. KT2355 aligns only specific image-processing methods; KT2305 imaging acquisition/clinical interpretation remains unmatched. The verified 15-EC research component places optional UCR research without making it a scheduled course or a clinical capstone equivalent. Unknown/disputed placement is outside all rows.

sourceFirstChallenge.test: Read actual functional anatomy medical-image work, pathophysiology clinical-case analysis, pharmacokinetic quantitative exercises, signal transforms, image-processing pipeline, robot-arm manipulation and consumer prototype work. Their distinct contributions are real, but they do not evidence clinical robotics, device certification, patient placements or integrated medical engineering.
sourceFirstChallenge.resolution: Retain qualification only with the broad biomedical/computational title and prominent training limits.
